about_the_game:
An “accident” causes you, a third-year college student, to lose part of your memory—including the English vocabulary you once mastered. Urgently needing to rebuild your word power to meet the demands of your future career, you join an experimental program called the “Ten-Thousand Words Club.” There, you encounter four beautiful girls whose fates become intertwined with your own.

Gameplay Overview

You begin by choosing a vocabulary book and setting up your own study plan, including your learning methods and the number of new and review words per day. By completing these study tasks, you earn virtual currency, increase your assistants’ affection levels, and unlock new story content.

*After finishing your daily study plan, you may continue learning and reviewing through additional features, or choose to work part-time or fight monsters in the virtual world to earn extra currency and experience. Whether “working” or “monster hunting,” both are vocabulary-based games designed for review. While playing, you strengthen your mastery of previously learned words. With the virtual currency you earn, you can purchase outfits, stockings, combat equipment, houses, and gifts for your assistants.

*The story evolves based on your choices and the affection levels of the assistants. If you wish to pursue your favorite assistant, select her more often as your active assistant, complete your self-designed study plans, and earn plenty of virtual currency to give her gifts.

*The game’s main antagonist has also set his sights on the four beautiful assistants and sees you as a rival, causing trouble throughout the story. But don’t worry—if your vocabulary skills are strong enough, the assistants will always stand by your side!

Game Features

*High Efficiency: Learning efficiency is the top priority. Gameplay never compromises the effectiveness of vocabulary learning.

*Multiple Motivation Systems: Virtual assistant companionship, word-based “girlfriend” development, multiple story endings, rewards from vocabulary mini-games, and a rich achievement system—all designed to continuously motivate you and keep your vocabulary study engaging.

*A More Scientific, User-Focused, and Personalized Learning Experience: We understand the flaws of traditional memorization methods. By making vocabulary learning more dynamic and moderately stimulating, we reduce boredom and drowsiness. We value user experience and never blindly recommend review workloads beyond your capacity. With multiple learning modes available, anything that can be customized is left in your hands and can be adjusted at any time.

*High-Quality Production: Full professional voice acting throughout the game, over 70 beautifully hand-drawn story CGs (including animated CGs), and several well-produced original theme and ending songs.

*Deep Immersion: You play as a character living in a virtual town, seamlessly blending learning with exploration. The town features day, dusk, and night cycles, allowing you to freely explore, fight monsters, trade, and engage in vocabulary battles—putting an end to dull memorization once and for all.

Trial Version Limitations:

In the trial version, you will be able to experience most of the game’s content, providing a very complete gameplay experience. Your game progress—including learned words, character level, equipment, items, affection level, and more—can be carried over to the full version (as long as you do not manually delete the local save files of the trial version on your computer).

However, the trial version has the following specific limitations:

  • In the trial version, story content can only be unlocked up to Prologue 3.

  • Some items, such as certain outfits and houses, are temporarily unavailable for purchase.

  • The free outfit-changing feature is temporarily unavailable.

  • The SS-rank Digimon Training Grounds are temporarily inaccessible.

Ten-Thousand Words Breaker: Word Girlfriend blends vocabulary learning with virtual romance, progression, and combat—making memorization fun, motivating, and efficient without sacrificing learning quality.
